analysis: Examined new ServingReadiness.swift (head 1-174), three new closed-vocabulary ProviderOperationalMessage cases (ProviderLogger.swift head 147-149), and new superviseServingAuthorization() call in capacityRefreshTick (ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift head 82). ServingReadiness is diagnostics-only: it derives operator-facing verdict text from the local daemon state file (coordinatorConnection, trust, authorization, appAttest) and does not gate serving; coordinator remains authoritative (TB-011, T-052, T-053, T-057). It interpolates coordinator-supplied reason strings (line 109/118/121) into status output; that is local operator display, not public unified log, so no ProviderLogger privacy-contract break. New log cases have no associated values, preserving the closed public vocabulary (only {cli} substitution). An integration risk: superviseServingAuthorization() implementation is not in this batch; the log text at line 149 implies the provider re-registers (closes/reopens) its connection after 15 min unauthorized. Next pass must verify: re-registration does not rotate/extend proof lifetime or reuse stale grants across endpoints (T-053, TB-011 endpoint-resumption protocol), cannot be triggered in a tight loop by an adversarial coordinator status (availability/T-057), does not drop in-flight decrypted work unsafely or leak plaintext (T-008, A-001), and that it runs on the loop actor without blocking App Attest challenge dispatch (2026-10-10 dispatch note). Also confirm hasCurrentAppAttestAuthorization is purely diagnostic here and not reused as a local serving gate. No concrete regression identified in supplied source.
